modules.name: Start Here — Understanding the FDE Role
modules.name_zh: 从这里开始：理解 FDE 角色
modules.purpose: Give readers who don't yet know what an FDE is a map before any engineering: what the role is accountable for, how it differs from neighboring roles, and which module builds the capability each stage of FDE delivery needs. Orientation only, no engineering detail.
modules.goal: give readers who don't yet know what a Forward Deployed Engineer is a map before any engineering begins: what the role is accountable for, how it differs from neighboring roles, and which module builds the capability each stage of FDE delivery needs. Orientation only, with no engineering detail; read it first whatever your background.
modules.notes: Required for every background; read first

lessons.label: What Is a Forward Deployed Engineer?
lessons.outcomes: Explain what an FDE is accountable for, place any FDE job on the four-responsibility model, and explain why the role needs engineering, AI, delivery and business context at once.

lessons.label: FDE vs. Adjacent Roles
lessons.outcomes: Compare an FDE with each neighboring role on responsibility rather than on who writes code, and use the three role tests to place a real job description.

lessons.label: The FDE Delivery Lifecycle & Handbook Map
lessons.label_zh: FDE 交付生命周期与手册地图
lessons.outcomes: Name the lifecycle stages in order, say which module builds the capability each stage needs, and pick a reading path through the handbook from your background.

modules.name: AI-Assisted Development & Software Systems Foundations
modules.name_zh: AI 辅助开发与软件系统基础
modules.purpose: Build a mental model of modern software systems for beginners or technically rusty learners, and enable them to read, run, modify, debug, and deploy code with AI coding tools. The focus is system understanding rather than syntax memorization.
modules.goal: help beginners or technically rusty learners build a mental model of modern software systems and use AI coding tools to read, run, modify, debug, and deploy code. The emphasis is not memorizing syntax, but understanding how systems work.
modules.notes: Skip mastered modules based on the entry assessment

lessons.label: AI Coding Workspace & Vibe Coding Collaboration
lessons.outcomes: Set up an AI-assisted development workspace; read and modify small codebases; explain what submitted code actually does.

lessons.label: How Modern Web Applications Actually Work
lessons.outcomes: Draw the architecture of a simple application and explain how a request flows through the frontend, backend, database, and external services.

lessons.label: API, Data & Systems Integration Foundations
lessons.outcomes: Read API documentation, call external services, inspect returned data, and diagnose whether integration failures come from authentication, networking, formatting, or business logic.

lessons.label: Git, Debugging, Testing & Security Basics
lessons.outcomes: Maintain a traceable code repository, diagnose common errors, and demonstrate basic security and testing awareness.

lessons.label: Docker, Containers, Cloud & Basic Deployment
lessons.outcomes: Understand core containerization and cloud deployment concepts; deploy an application using existing platforms and diagnose common deployment issues.

lessons.label: Reliability, Async Work & Scalability Basics
lessons.outcomes: Recognize reliability and scalability issues that appear when moving from demo to real usage, and judge when queues, retries, or concurrency controls are needed.

modules.name: AI Application Engineering
modules.purpose: Turn LLMs from “chat tools” into verifiable, integrable application capabilities. Use a Tutor / Customer Support RAG case to build foundations in prompting, RAG, tool calling, evaluation, and guardrails.
modules.goal: turn LLMs from “chat tools” into verifiable, integrable application capabilities. Use a Tutor / Customer Support RAG case to establish foundations in prompting, RAG, tool calling, evaluation, and guardrails.
modules.notes: Skip mastered modules based on the entry assessment

lessons.label: LLM Application Foundations: From Chat to Programmatic Use
lessons.outcomes: Call an LLM from code, explain model inputs and outputs, and understand that good chat behavior does not equal system reliability.

lessons.label: Prompting, Context & Structured Output
lessons.outcomes: Design reusable prompts and structured-output contracts, and explain why prompts may fail in different contexts.

lessons.label: RAG & Knowledge Bases: Tutor / Support Assistant
lessons.outcomes: Build a basic RAG assistant that cites sources, identifies knowledge gaps, and escalates to a human when evidence is insufficient.

lessons.label: Tool Calling & Deterministic Logic
lessons.outcomes: Separate model judgment from deterministic execution, design a verifiable tool, and enable the LLM to call it correctly.

lessons.label: AI Evaluation: Proving It Actually Works
lessons.outcomes: Build a minimum viable evaluation set, document failure cases, and use evidence rather than intuition to judge whether changes improve the system.

lessons.label: Safety, Guardrails & Human-in-the-Loop
lessons.outcomes: Define basic safety boundaries and human checkpoints for an AI application, without confusing “the model can answer” with “the model is allowed to act.”

modules.name: Agent Engineering — From Prompts to Scalable Agent Systems
modules.purpose: Define an agent as a job with real boundaries, give it reusable skills backed by code where needed, choose between a workflow, a single agent and multiple agents, and make its state, long-running work and failures manageable. An agent is not simply a prompt, and more agents are not automatically better.
modules.goal: define an agent as a job with real boundaries (Profile, with Knowledge kept separate), give it reusable Skills backed by code where steps must repeat exactly, choose between a workflow, a single agent and multiple agents, then make its state, long-running work and failures manageable. An agent is not merely a prompt, and more agents do not automatically mean a better system.
modules.notes: Skip mastered modules based on the entry assessment

lessons.label: Start with Profile.md: Define an Agent with Real Boundaries
lessons.outcomes: Define an agent with clear boundaries from business responsibilities rather than writing a one-line role prompt.

lessons.label: Skills: Decompose Agent Capabilities into Reusable Units
lessons.outcomes: Decompose a complex agent into maintainable, testable, reusable skills and identify where code is required.

lessons.label: Workflow, Single Agent, or Multi-Agent?
lessons.outcomes: Choose the simplest viable architecture based on task complexity and risk, and justify the design with business reasons rather than “multi-agent is more advanced.”

lessons.label: State, Memory & Context Persistence
lessons.outcomes: Design state and memory boundaries for agents, and distinguish “a lot of context” from reliable persistence.

lessons.label: Persistent Agents: Queues, Recovery, Concurrency & HITL
lessons.outcomes: Understand persistent-agent execution and explain how tasks are queued, recovered, deduplicated, and paused for human approval at critical points.

lessons.label: Agent Evaluation, Tracing & Debugging
lessons.outcomes: Locate failures within an agent workflow and use traces/evaluations—not endless prompt rewriting—to fix them.

modules.name: Enterprise Integration & Production AI
modules.purpose: Teach learners that real customer environments involve data, APIs, permissions, security, deployment, observability, cost, and reliability beyond prompts/agents, and develop judgment about when deeper engineering is required.
modules.goal: show that real customer environments involve data, APIs, permissions, security, deployment, observability, cost, and reliability beyond prompts and agents. Learners should know when deeper engineering is required.
modules.notes: Skip mastered modules based on the entry assessment

lessons.label: External APIs, MCP & Connector Design
lessons.outcomes: Explain the difference between APIs and MCP, and connect external data or actions to agents through clear, replaceable interfaces.

lessons.label: Authentication, Authorization, RBAC & Secrets
lessons.outcomes: Design a basic permission model and understand that prompts cannot replace real authentication and authorization controls.

lessons.label: Real-World Data: Quality, Freshness, Provenance & Entity Resolution
lessons.outcomes: Identify major risks in real data, design provenance/freshness/entity-alignment rules, and clearly state which conclusions remain unverified.

lessons.label: Reliability, Cost, Latency & Scale
lessons.outcomes: Make basic performance and cost trade-offs and recognize when a demo architecture can no longer support real users.

lessons.label: Deployment, CI/CD, Observability & Production Readiness
lessons.outcomes: Explain what an AI application still needs to move from a local demo to an internal pilot and production, and produce basic deployment/run evidence.

modules.name: FDE Discovery, Consulting & Delivery
modules.purpose: Train the core capabilities that distinguish FDEs from typical AI Engineers: entering ambiguous customer environments, finding the real problem, defining outcomes, managing scope, making technical/business trade-offs, and driving pilots, acceptance, handoff, and productization.
modules.goal: train the core capabilities that distinguish an FDE from a typical AI Engineer—entering ambiguous customer environments, finding the real problem, defining outcomes, managing scope, making technical/business trade-offs, and driving pilots, acceptance, handoff, and productization.
modules.notes: Skip mastered modules based on the entry assessment

lessons.label: The FDE Role & End-to-End Delivery Lifecycle
lessons.outcomes: Understand the full scope of FDE work, recognize that technical capability is only one part, and complete a personal skill-gap assessment.

lessons.label: Customer Discovery & Stakeholder Interviews
lessons.outcomes: Run a structured discovery session, identify key stakeholders, real problems, and information gaps, and produce reviewable interview notes.

lessons.label: As-Is / To-Be Workflow Mapping & Requirement Decomposition
lessons.outcomes: Translate ambiguous requests into clear business workflows and identify where AI should actually intervene.

lessons.label: Scope, PRD/SOW, Acceptance Criteria & Non-Goals
lessons.outcomes: Write an implementable and testable mini PRD/SOW and protect the project from unlimited scope creep.

lessons.label: Solution Architecture: Choose the Simplest Architecture That Works
lessons.outcomes: Choose the minimum viable architecture based on customer value, time, risk, and team capability, and explain how it can evolve later.

lessons.label: Demo, Feedback & Change Management
lessons.outcomes: Run a demo for non-technical stakeholders and clearly explain trade-offs when new requests appear instead of agreeing unconditionally.

lessons.label: Pilot, Value, Handoff & Productization
lessons.outcomes: Design both business and technical metrics for a pilot and use evidence to explain project value and uncertainty. Hand a project over so others can run it and extract reusable assets rather than keeping all knowledge in one person’s head.

modules.name: Four Representative FDE Use-Case Archetypes
modules.name_zh: 四个代表性 FDE 用例原型
modules.purpose: Use four realistic cases of increasing complexity to demonstrate the same FDE method repeatedly. Industry is the context; the goal is to understand why different business problems require different technical depth.
modules.goal: use four realistic cases of increasing complexity to repeatedly demonstrate the same FDE methodology. Industry is the context; the focus is understanding why different business problems require different levels of technical depth.
modules.notes: Skip mastered modules based on the entry assessment

lessons.label: Education Tutor / Customer Support: RAG Application
lessons.outcomes: Understand and build one of the simplest enterprise AI applications, and recognize when RAG alone is sufficient.

lessons.label: Content Operations: Multi-Stage Content Production Workflow
lessons.outcomes: Decompose a content-operations process into agents/workflows and understand that multi-agent value comes from separation of responsibilities, not agent count.

lessons.label: Healthcare Provider Research & Outreach: Data-Driven Prospecting
lessons.outcomes: Break target-customer research and outreach into a verifiable data/automation pipeline and know which information requires human confirmation.

lessons.label: Finance Research / Trading Desk: Complex Multi-Agent Decision Support
lessons.outcomes: Understand why complex agent systems need multiple roles, tools, freshness controls, memory, and evaluation, and design a simplified research desk.

modules.name: FDE End-to-End Practicum
modules.purpose: Learners choose an approved customer-style use case and complete a full FDE delivery from Discovery through Release/Handoff. This is the core job-search portfolio module and is not tied to a fixed number of weeks.
modules.goal: learners choose an approved customer-style use case and complete a full FDE delivery from Discovery through Release/Handoff. This is the core portfolio module and is not tied to a fixed number of weeks; learners can progress based on their available effort.
modules.notes: Skip mastered modules based on the entry assessment

lessons.label: Practicum Kickoff: Discovery & Project Selection
lessons.label_zh: 实战启动：需求发现与项目选择
lessons.outcomes: Produce an approved Problem Brief and Discovery Pack demonstrating that the project is worth designing and building.

lessons.label: Architecture & MVP Freeze
lessons.outcomes: Produce an executable MVP design and explain each architecture choice, technical debt item, and deferred feature.

lessons.label: Alpha Build: Complete the First End-to-End Happy Path
lessons.label_zh: Alpha 构建：打通第一条端到端主路径
lessons.outcomes: Complete a reproducible Alpha Release proving that the core business path runs from input to output.

lessons.label: Evaluation & Hardening
lessons.outcomes: Complete a Beta with evaluation results, a failure report, and prioritized reliability improvements—not just a successful demo path.

lessons.label: Pilot / Proxy User Testing & Release Candidate
lessons.label_zh: 试点 / 代理用户测试与候选发布版本
lessons.outcomes: Use real or proxy-user evidence to determine whether the system is worth continuing and complete a demonstrable Release Candidate.

lessons.label: Client Demo, Stakeholder Defense, Handoff & Postmortem
lessons.label_zh: 客户演示、利益相关方答辩、交接与复盘
lessons.outcomes: Complete an end-to-end FDE project suitable for interviews and a portfolio, demonstrating not only agent building but full delivery ownership.

modules.name: Career Preparation & FDE Interviews
modules.name_zh: 就业准备与 FDE 面试
modules.purpose: Turn real curriculum and practicum outputs into verifiable job-search evidence, and prepare for common FDE interviews in engineering, system design, problem decomposition, customer communication, and project deep dives.
modules.goal: turn real curriculum and practicum outputs into verifiable job-search evidence, and prepare for common FDE interviews covering engineering, system design, problem decomposition, customer communication, and project deep dives.
modules.notes: Skip mastered modules based on the entry assessment

lessons.label: Portfolio, Case Study & Resume Packaging
lessons.outcomes: Turn course outputs into a credible, explainable, and verifiable FDE resume and portfolio.

lessons.label: Coding / Debugging & System Design Interviews
lessons.label_zh: Coding / Debugging 与 System Design 面试
lessons.outcomes: Explain and modify code in interviews and complete practical system designs aligned with FDE work.

lessons.label: FDE Case: Problem Decomposition & Customer Simulation
lessons.label_zh: FDE Case：Problem Decomposition 与 Customer Simulation
lessons.outcomes: Structure ambiguous customer problems, propose verifiable solutions, and communicate with non-technical stakeholders.

lessons.label: Role Matching, Interview Narrative & Job-Search Strategy
lessons.label_zh: 岗位匹配、面试叙事与求职策略
lessons.outcomes: Define a personal job-market position, project narrative, and follow-up skill-gap roadmap, and identify which FDE/adjacent roles fit best.
